To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GAN training with unregularized Wasserstein loss does not always converge to a fixed point.

(1) GAN training with unregularized cross-entropy loss does not always converge, (2) GAN training is convergent for instance-noise regularization and zero-centered gradient penalties, (3) GAN training does not always converge for Wasserstein GANs and W-GAN-GP with a fixed number of discriminator updates, and (4) GANs with simplified gradient penalties converge to a local optimum.

(i) GAN training with regularization methods that penalize the norm of the discriminator’s gradient with respect to the input (such as instance noise, WGAN-GP, and simplified gradient penalties) converge, while (ii) GAN training without such penalties may not converge, even if the generator distribution is absolutely continuous with respect to the data distribution.

the stability issues of GAN training are not due to a lack of regularization, but rather due to a lack in local convergence guarantees.
